identity.title: ThinKV: Thought-Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Efficient Reasoning Models

problem.claim: Long-output reasoning causes KV-cache growth that can overwhelm GPU memory during extended chain-of-thought generation.

contributions.claim: ThinKV is a thought-adaptive KV-cache compression framework that combines importance-based token quantization with progressive eviction from less critical thoughts.
The authors design a kernel extending PagedAttention to reuse memory slots of evicted tokens and avoid compaction overhead.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish ThinKV through thought-adaptive compression based on attention-revealed thought types, together with hybrid quantization–eviction and memory-slot reuse.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report near-lossless accuracy using less than 5% of the original KV cache across DeepSeek-R1-Distill, GPT-OSS, and NVIDIA AceReason on mathematics and coding benchmarks.
The authors report up to 5.8× higher inference throughput than stated-of-the-art baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Extended chain-of-thought increases KV-cache memory pressure.
ThinKV adapts token precision and eviction to thought importance as reasoning evolves.
A PagedAttention-based kernel reuses evicted-token memory slots without compaction overhead.
Experiments on reasoning models and mathematics/coding benchmarks report near-lossless accuracy, extreme cache reduction, and higher throughput.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links attention sparsity to distinct thought types, then maps thought importance to precision and eviction decisions.

lessons.interpretation: A resource-management method can become more specific by tying its control policy to an interpretable property of the workload.
lessons.application: When proposing adaptive inference, identify a measurable workload signal and explicitly map its levels to distinct resource actions.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the signal is unstable, unavailable at runtime, or not shown to track the target resource need.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the baselines, exact accuracy differences behind “near-lossless,” benchmark sizes, or evaluation settings.
It does not report separate contributions of quantization, eviction, or the kernel to the stated results.
